quote: I don't know, like, a ton of the details, especially for the roofs, but our, our specialist would know know all about that for you.
stewart_read: Customer directly asked about Ion's roofing program — a strong cross-sell signal — and the rep acknowledged the program exists but did not bridge it with any urgency or route it in real time.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be seen as correctly deferring to the specialist per setter_scope_discipline, but the schema calls for an active bridge ('let me flag that for our roofing team'), not just a passive mention.
coaching_implication: Train reps to treat roofing questions as an immediate co-route trigger, not just an FYI — capture roof age/material mentioned earlier (garage roof ~5 years, house ~20) and hand that to the roofing team.

quote: Okay. Perfect. And the house is probably 20.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers the house roof is ~20 years old right after mentioning the garage roof is newer — this is exactly the kind of detail that should trigger a roofing bridge given the customer later asks about roofing directly.
coaching_implication: Rep should have flagged the older roof age as a potential roofing-program trigger before the customer had to ask himself two minutes later.

quote: I would have to get it from the renter.
stewart_read: The bill was never captured live; the booking proceeded on a promise to text the tenant later, which is a real structural condition on the appointment, not a resolved objection.
coaching_implication: Handoff brief must flag this as an unresolved condition — closer needs the bill before a real design can be shown.

stewart_read: Rep never got a firm 'is that fair?' handshake after landing 11 AM Wednesday — the word 'tentatively' from the customer was left unaddressed.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged pushing further risked losing the soft yes given the customer's repeated 'play it by ear' framing — a strategic soft-touch. But the schema still requires a verbal handshake to protect show rate.
coaching_implication: Rep should follow a hedge like 'tentatively' with a direct confirm: 'Great, so we'll plan on 11 Wednesday — does that work for your calendar?' to convert the hedge into a real commitment.

quote: $16 summertime bill sounds really good with me. Yeah.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strongly positive past-solar-savings memory unprompted — a gift the rep could use to anchor excitement toward the new system.
coaching_implication: Rep should have echoed this back later when discussing the new $400 bill to build a before/after contrast ('remember that $16 bill — let's get you back there').

quote: I think it's, like, 400 a month.
stewart_read: The $400 bill was captured but the rep's response ('Oh, wow. Okay.') was a filed reaction, not a flip into emotional alignment against the utility.
coaching_implication: Rep should reflect the $400 back as the actual expense being replaced, tying it to the earlier $16 bill memory for maximum contrast.
